\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Scratch-Word Comparison Loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_scmp}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_scmp}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DblAt, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.half, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jodd_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jodd_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_0, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_6, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_bit, Complexity.bits_eq_cons, Complexity.dblAt_cons}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a Boolean string, $B$ a natural-number register bound, and $q$ a rational
number. For every natural number $w$ and register state $\sigma$, suppose the scratch
register equals $w$, every register is at most $B$, and the input pointer plus twice the
length of the binary expansion of the scratch value plus two is at most $B$. If the
binary expansion of the scratch value is doubled at the input pointer, then the
configuration at the comparison-exit state, with the pointer advanced by that amount and
the scratch register cleared, has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability
$q$. If that doubled-word pattern does not occur, suppose that for every pointer and
scratch-register value at most $B$, the configuration at the fallback state with those
values has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. Then the
comparison-loop configuration with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics
with acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Transition through the target comparison]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_tcmp}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_tcmp}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.half, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jodd_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jodd_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_0, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_6, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_bit, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_len, Complexity.PlainAt, Complexity.bits_eq_cons, Complexity.plainAt_cons}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Let
$\sigma$ be a register state and $w$ a natural number with $\sigma.tmp=w$, all registers
of $\sigma$ at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, and $\sigma.p\le |x|$. If the word of binary
digits of $w$ occurs at position $\sigma.p$ in $x$ and ends exactly at the end of $x$,
assume that the program started at the target-test stage with pointer $|x|$ and scratch
value zero has semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If this occurrence condition
fails, assume that for every $p',tmp'\le B$, the program started at the next search
stage with pointer $p'$ and scratch value $tmp'$ has semantics with acceptance
probability $q$. Then the program started at the target-comparison stage in state
$\sigma$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Candidate Search Loop Invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_ssearch}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_ssearch}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DblAt, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.cpEx, Complexity.LogProg.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.ups_cp, Complexity.LogProg.ups_rej, Complexity.LogProg.ups_scmp, Turing.length_bits_le_self}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a Boolean string, $B$ a natural-number register bound, and $q$ a rational
number. For every natural number $dd$ and register state $\sigma$, suppose the vertex
count minus the candidate counter, with truncated natural subtraction, equals $dd$;
every register is at most $B$; the candidate counter $u$ is at most the vertex count
$n$; the current-vertex register is zero; and the saved pointer $q_0$ plus $2n+2$ is at
most $B$. For every $j\ge u$ with $j<n$, if the binary expansion of $j$ is doubled at
position $q_0$ in $x$, then the configuration at the specified state with candidate and
current-vertex registers set to $j$, pointer set to $q_0+2|\mathrm{bits}(j)|+2$, and
scratch register cleared has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If
there is no $j$ with $u\le j<n$ whose binary expansion is doubled at position $q_0$ in
$x$, then $q=0$. The configuration at the search-loop state with register state $\sigma$
has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Search for a target encoding]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_tsearch}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_tsearch}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.cpEx, Complexity.LogProg.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.ups_cp, Complexity.LogProg.ups_rej, Complexity.LogProg.ups_tcmp, Complexity.PlainAt}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Let
$d$ be a natural number and $\sigma$ a register state such that $\sigma.n-\sigma.u=d$,
every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.u\le\sigma.n$, $\sigma.t=0$,
$\sigma.q\le |x|$, and $2|x|+2\le B$. Assume that for every $j$ with $\sigma.u\le
j<\sigma.n$ whose binary word occurs at position $\sigma.q$ in $x$ and ends exactly at
the end of $x$, the program started at the candidate-processing stage with $u=t=j$,
pointer $|x|$, and scratch value zero has semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If
there is no such $j$, assume $q=0$. Then the program started at the search stage in
state $\sigma$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}
